takeaways.label: Revenue up 32% YoY, margins steady
takeaways.text: Q2 revenue hit ₹2,030 crore with EBITDA at 27.1%, the higher end of the mid-20s guidance band, while H1 cash generation reached ₹1,010 crore.

takeaways.label: Export orders are the breakout story
takeaways.text: H1 export orders of ₹1,040 crore already nearly match all of FY26, driven by broad-based demand and supply chain stretch, not a single large related-party deal.

takeaways.label: The HVDC thesis is intact but still future-dated
takeaways.text: Management expects 2–3 HVDC projects next year and significant execution only from FY28 onward; localization of valves and controls is complete, but the next phase of sub-component work is just beginning.

takeaways.label: Supply chain is the number one stated risk
takeaways.text: Global demand and geopolitical disturbances keep supply chain stretched, and management calls it something that "can have a very severe impact on operations."

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the Barmer HVDC order books this quarter as expected, whether the U.S. data-center RPT order closes in H2, and any concrete timeline on the three HVDC projects awaiting NCT clearance.

points.label: Q2 order intake
points.text: of ₹2,440 crore was driven entirely by regular orders with no one-offs; key wins spanned pumped storage, AP transmission, TBCB projects in HP and AP, plus export momentum across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa and grid automation.

points.label: Export orders
points.text: reached 21% of Q2 intake and 29% of H1 intake; the ₹1,040 crore H1 export figure, mostly from related parties, already approaches the full FY26 total of ₹1,180 crore, driven by many smaller orders across geographies rather than a single large RPT.

points.label: Small-order export drivers
points.text: include increased investment in many geographies, stretched global supply chains creating additional opportunity, and factory certifications worked on over the last year now yielding results.

points.label: Base orders target
points.text: of ₹7,000–8,000 crore for the full year is maintained, and management is confident this year will be much stronger than last year, with a strong domestic pipeline over the next 4–5 months.

points.label: Barmer HVDC
points.text: is expected to see significant booking this quarter; the company is already the lowest bidder on Power Grid's Barmer tender.

points.label: One RPT approval lapsed
points.text: because the customer put the project on hold due to operational planning delays; the order was never booked and is not part of the backlog, and management is unsure whether the hold lifts in 6, 8 or 12 months.

points.label: A new material RPT approval
points.text: was secured for a U.S. entity for ~$151 million of goods exports from India, valid until 15 May 2027; if closed in H2, full-year export growth will be very significant.

quotes.text: Sandeep Zanzaria: "We have a very strong pipeline of HVDC going forward. We expect minimum 2 to 3 projects to come next year."

points.label: Q2 revenue
points.text: grew 32% YoY to ₹2,030 crore; H1 revenue of ~₹3,860 crore grew 35% YoY, driven by strong execution and backlog conversion.

points.label: Export revenues
points.text: were 32% of Q2 revenue and 31% of H1 revenue; ₹1,200 crore of export backlog was executed in H1 against a ₹1,700 crore order book at FY26-end, with most flow orders being short-cycle while past large projects carried 3–5 year delivery timelines.

points.label: Services and software
points.text: share of total revenue may have dropped as a ratio because equipment order booking, including HVDC, has been very strong, though every business is growing YoY; management declined to give a breakup.

points.label: Commissioning highlights
points.text: included a 400kV substation for NEA Nepal, 400kV GIS for GETCO, 765kV reactors for PGCIL, a 765kV generator transformer for NUPPL, GIS at Narela Delhi, plus export jobs in Spain and Senegal.

points.label: HVDC execution
points.text: will not contribute significantly this financial year or even in FY27-28; the significant part of HVDC execution starts from FY28 onward.

points.label: Revenue growth trajectory
points.text: with the current backlog of ₹21,400 crore plus the HVDC L1 position supports average revenue growth of more than 30% over the next three years, per management.

points.label: Gross margin
points.text: came in at 44.5% for Q2, a level management says is not exceptional and was achieved last financial year too; quarter-on-quarter variation reflects operational execution, domestic vs export mix, project vs products mix, and different product components.

points.label: EBITDA margin
points.text: was 27.1% in Q2, at the higher end of the mid-20s guidance band; H1 EBITDA of ~26.2% was also in line, with resilience in gross margin maintained despite mix changes.

points.label: Other expenses
points.text: grew ~38% in the quarter, including some operational forex loss, but overall growth was in line with revenue and there is no one-off provisioning concern.

points.label: Employee costs
points.text: are growing at a rate less than revenue growth; the increase is driven by headcount addition to execute 30%+ revenue growth and normal salary increments, with nothing exceptional in the number.

points.label: Export vs domestic margins
points.text: continue to show export orders carrying ~500 bps better margins than domestic ones, consistent with past commentary.

points.label: Pricing pressure
points.text: on regular high-voltage transformers is "very little, not significant," though slight pressure exists even after accounting for copper price increases of more than 50% in one year.

points.label: Operating leverage
points.text: is the core margin story: with only ~₹1,000 crore of capex, most of it in existing plants where land is already owned, the company can execute the entire backlog and generate significant absolute EPS growth and high ROE; management urges focus on absolute profitability and ROE rather than gross margin% or EBITDA% components.

quotes.text: Sushil Kumar: "With that kind of revenue execution, while we are expanding at our factories, it's only 1,000 crore of capex. So, with that small investment, we are able to execute this entire backlog. Which means that without looking at gross margin% or EBITDA%, there will be a significant operating leverage that kicks in leading to growth in the absolute earnings per share with the same amount of capital."

points.label: HVDC pipeline
points.text: remains a key focus area; management expects a minimum of 2–3 HVDC projects to come next year, though no HVDC tender has been issued since Barmer, so competitive intensity cannot yet be assessed.

points.label: Three HVDC projects
points.text: (two Barmer, one Navadiya) have not yet been cleared by the National Committee on Transmission and are expected to happen in 2027 next year.

points.label: HVDC localization
points.text: is now complete for transformers, valves and controls, all manufactured in India after the capex program; the next phase will work on localizing components from subcontractors and sub-vendors, a journey that will proceed component by component with local Indian manufacturers.

points.label: 765 kV bushing localization
points.text: is currently mostly imported due to limited Indian manufacturing capacity, but capacity expansion is ongoing and localization is expected in times to come.

points.label: STATCOM ordering
points.text: is expected to see a sizable portion ordered in Q4.

points.label: 1150 kV corridor
points.text: is still a bit away; it is too early to quantify the TAM as it depends on how many projects come per year and the pipeline.

quotes.text: Sandeep Zanzaria: "At one point of time, a large part of the transformers and 100% of valves and controls are coming from outside. But with whatever capex we have done or whatever capex is under progress, all these things have been localized."

points.label: Data center traction
points.text: is expected to strengthen materially from Q4 or most probably next year, when larger-size data centers at 400 kV and 765 kV begin coming; the current India data center TAM is small at 200–300 MW and 220 kV.

points.label: Data center demand risk
points.text: in India is not seen as significant; management believes these companies have the capacity to raise capital and build data centers for AI.

points.label: TBCB intrastate pipeline
points.text: is growing as many states have expressed intent to move 400 kV and 765 kV expansion to TBCB mode, though it is difficult to quantify a yearly number.

points.label: TBCB equipment ordering
points.text: from the ₹1 lakh crore pipeline is hard to predict for this year because developer timelines have extended to 24–30 months from 18–21 months, and a float is created post-award.

points.label: GEC III corridor
points.text: opportunity is largely already covered under the CEA electricity plan; market guidance remains unchanged from the recent investor meet presentation.

points.label: Domestic capacity expansions
points.text: announced by companies are mostly for export markets, not domestic; if they follow what they are saying, management does not see too much pressure coming on domestic market prices.

points.label: Competitive intensity
points.text: in exports with large Indian non-MNC players has not been visible; management says it is very difficult to predict impact directionally.

quotes.text: Sandeep Zanzaria: "There's a lot of capacity expansions, what companies have announced... they're putting up capacity mostly for the export market, not for the domestic market. And if they follow what they are saying, then I don't see too much pressure coming on the domestic market prices."

points.label: GE Vernova Global's acquisition of Trench
points.text: was announced two days before the call and is expected to close in the later part of FY27; management views it as very positive for India, providing larger control over the supply chain for HVDC and STATCOM, making the company more competitive and secure.

points.label: Trench impact on delivery timelines
points.text: is not a given: Trench has its own pipeline and delivery commitments and will not simply divert all output to internal GE Vernova factories.

points.label: Trench manufacturing expansion in India
points.text: is too early to comment on, as the acquisition was announced only two days prior.

points.label: Supply chain
points.text: remains the number one risk; global demand is high, geopolitical disturbances keep emerging, and it can have a very severe impact on operations.

points.label: Capex program
points.text: of ~₹1,000 crore for capacity expansion is progressing, with ~20% already incurred; management is continuously evaluating the market and will not shy away from investing further in the country if needed.

points.label: Cash utilization
points.text: options are being evaluated to optimize shareholder returns; net zero debt is maintained with total cash at ₹3,250 crore.

quotes.text: Sandeep Zanzaria: "Supply chain today is one of the things which can have a very severe impact on the operations."

items.title: 30%+ revenue growth guide
items.text: Management targets revenue growth above 30% annually over the next 3-4 years, matching the pace of the last 3-4, supported by the ₹21,440 crore backlog (over three years of FY26 revenue) and the Barmer HVDC L1 position. Only ~₹1,000 crore of capex is needed to get there, so most incremental revenue drops through as operating leverage.

items.title: Barmer ±800 kV HVDC L1
items.text: Power Grid intimated L1 status by letter dated 7 Sep 2026 for a 6,000 MW, ±800 kV HVDC terminal station (Barmer II-South Kalamb), with booking expected in the coming quarter and execution mainly over FY28-FY30. The company's addressable equipment share in a typical HVDC project is 40-60%, so a single win of this class can add ₹3,000-5,000 crore of revenue in a peak execution year.

items.title: Adani Khavda-South Olpad HVDC order
items.text: A contract dated 20 Dec 2025 from Adani Energy Solutions covers a 2,500 MW, ±500 kV VSC terminal station plus transformers, with the zero date already started and a ~4-year execution timeline. Most revenue lands from FY29 as material supply begins, adding a private-sector HVDC stream that flows fully through the Indian entity.

items.title: HVDC tender pipeline beyond Barmer
items.text: Management expects 2-3 HVDC projects to come to tender in 2027, with ~10 Rajasthan links of ~6 GW each planned through 2035-36 and the new National Electricity Plan targeting 33 GW of new bipole capacity by 2032. Each additional award compounds the FY29+ execution ramp already visible in the backlog.

items.title: Chandrapur HVDC refurbishment
items.text: A Letter of Award dated 17 Dec 2025 from Power Grid covers upgrading the 2x500 MW Chandrapur back-to-back link - India's first HVDC refurbishment order. LCC links installed 20-25 years ago form a repeat refurbishment pipeline, with Pisoli and Pusauli already in discussion.

items.title: HVDC valve and controls localization
items.text: A ₹140 crore investment restarts the Pallavaram (Chennai) LCC valve line and adds a VSC-STATCOM valve line plus a new Noida HVDC controls facility, with the valve factory due for commissioning. This makes the end HVDC product fully Indian-manufactured, cuts import dependence and builds an export base for global HVDC work.

items.title: US data-center transformer exports
items.text: A ~$151 million related-party approval for exporting transformers to the US, valid till 15 May 2027, is under negotiation with conclusion expected in H2 FY27. Vadodara is GE Vernova's only higher-rating transformer plant in Asia, so Prolec's large US transformer orders should also route Indian supply.

items.title: STATCOM ordering wave
items.text: A sizable portion of India's STATCOM awards is expected in Q4 FY27, with CEA recommending STATCOMs at all future 400/765 kV substations handling renewables. The new Pallavaram VSC-STATCOM valve line means the company can supply these orders from India.

items.title: Vallam disconnector restart
items.text: A ₹55 crore board-approved facility at Vallam restarts disconnector and drives production (currently nil capacity), with first production tentatively by December 2026 and the balance by end of '27. 765 kV substations were practically all equipped with GE Vernova disconnectors, so this recaptures returning domestic demand and adds margin via backward integration.
